intro: The probability of a count combines the number of compatible sequences with the likelihood of each sequence. Log space keeps those factors manageable.
task: Compute the log probability of exactly successes events in trials independent Bernoulli observations.
requirements: trials is an integer in [0,1000000] and successes is an integer in [0,trials]. probability is a scalar in [0,1].
Return log(combination(trials,successes))+successes*log(probability)+(trials-successes)*log(1-probability). Use log-gamma for the combination and skip zero-count terms.
An endpoint probability is valid only when the requested count is possible; otherwise raise ValueError instead of returning negative infinity. Zero trials returns zero for every valid probability.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: A count can occur through many ordered sequences; the combinatorial term accounts for all of them.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Skip terms whose event count is zero before taking endpoint logarithms, and reject impossible positive-count events.

explanation: The binomial coefficient counts which trial positions could contain the observed successes. Omitting it computes one particular sequence probability rather than the probability of the count.
Zero observations contribute no evidence. Endpoint probabilities need explicit handling so that a zero count times log(0) does not produce an undefined intermediate value.
